levels.name: Beginner
levels.desc: Greetings, ser & estar, ordering in a bar, your city

lessons.title: I am…
lessons.explain: Ser means "to be" for identity: who you are, where you're from, your job. yo soy (I am), tú eres (you are, informal), él / ella / usted es (he / she is, you are formal). Spanish often drops the pronoun: "Soy Ana" is enough. In Spain tú is used a lot, even with strangers your age.

lessons.title: We are, they are
lessons.explain: Plural forms: nosotros somos (we are), vosotros sois (you all are, informal: in Spain this is the normal way to talk to friends), ellos / ellas son (they are). Ustedes son is the formal "you all", used with customers or older people.

exercises.en: María and Pedro are from Bilbao.

lessons.title: Reading: Lucía introduces herself
lessons.translation: Hi! My name is Lucía. I'm from Seville, in Spain. I'm an English student. My friend Tom is from London. Nice to meet you!

lessons.title: What time is it?
lessons.explain: Use es la una for 1 o'clock (singular) and son las + number for the rest: son las tres. Add y media (half past), y cuarto (quarter past) or menos cuarto (quarter to). "At" a time is a la / a las: a las ocho.
examples: La clase es a las nueve.

lessons.title: The and a
lessons.point: el / la / los / las · un / una
lessons.explain: Every noun is masculine or feminine. Most nouns ending in -o are masculine (el libro) and most ending in -a are feminine (la casa). "The": el, la, los, las. "A / some": un, una, unos, unas. Watch out for exceptions like el día and la mano.
examples: Tengo un perro y una gata.
I have a (male) dog and a (female) cat.

exercises.en: Good morning. How's the day going?

lessons.title: My, your, his
lessons.explain: Possessives go before the noun: mi (my), tu (your, informal), su (his / her / your formal / their). Add -s for plurals: mis hermanos (my siblings). Note tú (you) has an accent, but tu (your) doesn't.
examples: His / her / their parents are from Galicia.

lessons.title: Verbs ending in -ar
lessons.explain: Regular -ar verbs drop -ar and add: -o (yo), -as (tú), -a (él / ella / usted), -amos (nosotros), -áis (vosotros), -an (ellos / ustedes). Hablar → hablo, hablas, habla, hablamos, habláis, hablan. In Spain you'll use the vosotros form with friends all the time.

lessons.title: Ordering politely
lessons.explain: In a Spanish bar, the most natural way to order is ¿Me pone…? (could you get me…?) or ¿Me pones…? with tú. Quiero (I want) and me gustaría (I would like) also work. Ask for the bill with La cuenta, por favor, or ¿Cuánto es?
examples: ¿Me pone un café con leche, por favor?
Could I have a coffee with milk, please?
Una caña y una ración de patatas bravas.
A small beer and a portion of patatas bravas.

exercises.fill: ¿Me ＿ un zumo de naranja, por favor?
exercises.en: Could I have an orange juice, please?
I'd like a table for two.

lessons.title: Verbs ending in -er and -ir
lessons.explain: -er verbs: -o, -es, -e, -emos, -éis, -en (comer → como, comes, come, comemos, coméis, comen). -ir verbs are the same except nosotros -imos and vosotros -ís (vivir → vivimos, vivís).

lessons.title: I have
lessons.explain: Tener (to have) is irregular: tengo, tienes, tiene, tenemos, tenéis, tienen. Spanish also uses tener for age (Tengo veinte años = I'm twenty) and feelings like hunger (Tengo hambre = I'm hungry).

lessons.title: Where is it?
lessons.explain: Use estar for where something is: ¿Dónde está el museo? = Where is the museum? (estoy, estás, está, estamos, estáis, están). Use hay for "there is / there are": Hay un banco aquí = There's a bank here.
examples: Hay una farmacia en la calle Mayor.
There's a pharmacy on Calle Mayor.

lessons.title: Going places
lessons.explain: Ir (to go) is irregular: voy, vas, va, vamos, vais, van. Use a for "to", and a + el contracts to al: Voy al museo (I'm going to the museum), Vamos a la playa (We're going to the beach).
examples: Are you going to the party?
Let's go / We're going to the beach.

exercises.en: Are you going to the station?

lessons.title: I like…
lessons.explain: Gustar works backwards: the thing you like is the subject. Me gusta + one thing or a verb (Me gusta el café, Me gusta bailar). Me gustan + plural things (Me gustan los perros). Te gusta = you like, le gusta = he / she likes.

lessons.title: Adjectives agree
lessons.point: un chico alto · una chica alta
lessons.explain: Adjectives usually go after the noun and match it in gender and number: el coche rojo, la casa roja, los coches rojos. Adjectives ending in -e or a consonant don't change for gender: un libro grande, una casa grande.

lessons.title: Ser or estar?
lessons.explain: Both mean "to be". Ser is for what something IS: identity, origin, job, character (Es alto, Es de Cádiz). Estar is for location and temporary states or feelings (Está en casa, Estoy cansado). Compare: Es aburrido (he's boring) vs Está aburrido (he's bored).

lessons.title: I'm going to…
lessons.explain: To talk about plans, use ir + a + infinitive: Voy a comer (I'm going to eat), Vamos a ver una película (We're going to watch a movie). It's the easiest way to talk about the future.
examples: ¿Qué vas a hacer el fin de semana?
What are you going to do this weekend?
We're going to travel to Asturias.

exercises.en: What are you going to do?
We're going to watch a movie.

lessons.title: Reading: Diego's weekend
lessons.translation: On Saturday Diego goes to the beach with his friends. They eat paella in a small restaurant. On Sunday he's going to rest at home and read a book.

questions.q: Where does Diego go on Saturday?
What will Diego do on Sunday?

lessons.title: Talking like a local
lessons.explain: Spaniards chat casually: ¿Qué tal? (how's it going?), ¡No me digas! (no way! lit. don't tell me), ¡Venga! (come on! / OK then!), and ¿Quedamos? (shall we meet up?). Friends call each other tío / tía, and use vosotros for groups.
examples: How's it going, dude? All good?
¿Quedamos a las ocho en la terraza?
Shall we meet at eight on the terrace?

exercises.en: How's it going, girl? All good?
Shall we meet up tomorrow for a drink?

levels.name: Elementary
levels.desc: Past tenses, routines, shopping, the future

lessons.title: Today I have…
lessons.explain: In Spain, the perfect tense is used for things that happened today, this week, this year, or ever: haber (he, has, ha, hemos, habéis, han) + participle. Participles: -ar → -ado (hablado), -er / -ir → -ido (comido, vivido). Hoy he comido paella = I had paella today.
examples: Have you ever been to Seville?
Esta semana hemos ido al cine.
This week we've been to the cinema.

exercises.en: Today I had lunch at home.
This morning we've worked a lot.

lessons.title: Irregular participles
lessons.explain: Some common verbs have irregular participles: hacer → hecho, ver → visto, decir → dicho, escribir → escrito, volver → vuelto, poner → puesto, abrir → abierto, romper → roto.
examples: They've already come back from holiday.

exercises.en: What have you done this weekend?

lessons.title: The simple past
lessons.explain: For finished times (ayer, el lunes pasado, en 2019) Spain uses the simple past. -ar: -é, -aste, -ó, -amos, -asteis, -aron (hablé, hablaste, habló…). -er / -ir: -í, -iste, -ió, -imos, -isteis, -ieron (comí, comiste, comió…). Watch the accents: hablo (I speak) vs habló (he spoke).
examples: Yesterday I spoke with my mother.
El verano pasado viajamos a Galicia.
Last summer we travelled to Galicia.
What did you guys eat last night?

exercises.en: Where did you guys live last year?
Last summer we travelled to Galicia.

lessons.title: Irregular simple past
lessons.explain: Very common irregulars: ser / ir → fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron (same forms!). tener → tuve, hacer → hice (él hizo), estar → estuve, poder → pude, venir → vine, decir → dije (ellos dijeron). These irregular forms have no accents.
examples: I went to Granada in May.
What did you do on Saturday?
Tuvimos un problema con el coche.
We had a problem with the car.

exercises.en: On Monday I went to the doctor.
What did you do on Saturday?

lessons.title: Reading: a trip to Granada
lessons.translation: Last month I went to Granada with my sister. We visited the Alhambra in the morning, and in the afternoon we ate tapas in the Albaicín. The tapas were free with the drink. It was a lovely trip!

questions.q: Who did the writer travel with?
What did they visit in the morning?
What was special about the tapas?
options: They were free with the drink
questions.answer: They were free with the drink

lessons.title: Used to / was -ing
lessons.explain: The imperfect describes the past: habits, background, how things were. -ar: -aba, -abas, -aba, -ábamos, -abais, -aban. -er / -ir: -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían. Only three irregulars: ser (era), ir (iba), ver (veía).
examples: De pequeño, vivía en un pueblo.
As a child, I lived in a village.
Mi abuela siempre cocinaba los domingos.
My grandmother always cooked on Sundays.
It was a very pretty house.

exercises.en: As a child, I used to play football.

exercises.fill: Siempre ＿ a la playa en verano. (ir, nosotros)
exercises.en: We always used to go to the beach in summer.
What did you guys use to do as kids?

lessons.title: Which past?
lessons.explain: Indefinido = a finished action (Llegué a las ocho). Imperfecto = the background or a habit (Llovía, Siempre llegaba tarde). Together: Cuando llegué, llovía = When I arrived, it was raining.
examples: Cuando llegué a casa, mi hermano dormía.
When I got home, my brother was sleeping.
Leía un libro cuando sonó el móvil.
I was reading a book when the phone rang.

exercises.en: When I got home, it was raining.
I was reading when the phone rang.
I used to live in Valencia.
When I arrived, my brother was sleeping.

lessons.title: Reflexive verbs
lessons.point: me levanto, te duchas, se acuesta…
lessons.explain: Reflexive verbs use a pronoun that matches the subject: me, te, se, nos, os, se. Levantarse → me levanto, te levantas, se levanta, nos levantamos, os levantáis, se levantan. Some change their stem: acostarse → me acuesto, despertarse → me despierto.
examples: What time do you guys go to bed?
Mi hermano se ducha por la noche.

exercises.en: What time do you go to bed?
Do you guys wake up early?

lessons.title: Bigger, better
lessons.explain: más + adjective + que = more … than; menos … que = less … than; tan … como = as … as. Irregulars: bueno → mejor, malo → peor. Esta chaqueta es más barata que esa = This jacket is cheaper than that one.
examples: Madrid es más grande que Sevilla.
Este jersey es tan bonito como ese.
This sweater is as nice as that one.

exercises.fill: El tren es más rápido ＿ el autobús.
exercises.en: The train is faster than the bus.
This one is as expensive as that one.

exercises.fill: Esta tienda es ＿ que la otra. (better)
exercises.en: This shop is better than the other one.
Do you have a bigger size?

lessons.title: It and them
lessons.explain: Direct object pronouns replace a thing or person: lo (it / him), la (it / her), los, las (them). They go before the verb: ¿La chaqueta? La compro = The jacket? I'll buy it. With infinitives they can attach: Voy a comprarla.
examples: ¿Te gusta este jersey? Sí, me lo llevo.
Do you like this sweater? Yes, I'll take it.
¿Tienes las llaves? No, no las tengo.
Do you have the keys? No, I don't have them.

exercises.en: The tickets? I haven't bought them.
This T-shirt… I'm going to buy it.

lessons.title: Do it!
lessons.explain: Commands for tú: use the él form of the present (habla, come, escribe). For vosotros: change the final -r of the infinitive to -d (hablad, comed, escribid). Irregular tú commands: ven, haz, pon, di, sal, ten, ve, sé.
examples: Gira a la derecha y sigue recto.
Turn right and go straight on.

lessons.title: I will…
lessons.explain: Add the endings to the whole infinitive: -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis, -án (hablaré, comerás, vivirá). Irregular stems: tener → tendré, hacer → haré, poder → podré, salir → saldré, venir → vendré, decir → diré, querer → querré.
examples: Tomorrow it will rain in the north.
El año que viene viviré en Madrid.
Next year I'll live in Madrid.
Will you guys come to the party?

exercises.en: On Saturday we'll have a party.
Next year I'll live in Madrid.

lessons.title: Reading: looking for a flat
lessons.translation: My name is Sara and next month I'll move to Madrid. I'm looking for a shared flat near the metro. I don't want to pay more than 500 euros a month. Yesterday I saw one in Lavapiés, but it was very small and had no windows.

questions.q: What was wrong with the flat in Lavapiés?
options: It was small and had no windows
It was far from the metro
questions.answer: It was small and had no windows
